newsitem.title: USA: U.S. search team arrives in North Korea.
newsitem.headline: U.S. search team arrives in North Korea.

text.p: A team of 10 U.S. experts arrived in North Korea on Tuesday to begin joint search and recovery operations for remains of Americans missing in action from the 1950-53 Korean War, the Pentagon said.

"The team arrived in Unsan County in northwest North Korea this morning. Their first task is to set up a base camp, from which suspected burial sites will be surveyed and eventually excavated," the announcement said.
Several hundred Americans are known to have been lost in Unsan County in fierce combat between U.S. and Chinese forces diring the war.
North Korea agreed in May to the joint POW/MIA search after a similar search last July found the remains of a U.S. soldier in Unsan County. He was identified and returned to his family for burial.
"If American remains are located, they will be returned to the United States for forensic identification," the Defence Department said.
Follow-on excavations in Unsan County are scheduled for August and October.
The Pentagon announcement said two of the 10 team members from the Defence and State Departments would remain in Pyongyang during the mission to facilitate communications with the field operation.
The trip by the POW/MIA experts illustrates a slow warming trend in relations between the United States and North Korea.
With four-way peace talks involving the United States, North Korea, South Korea and China less than one month away, the United States on Monday doubled its food aid to North Korea.

Following the latest urgent appeal by the U.N. World Food Programme, Washington pledged $27 million in food aid, bringing to $52 million its contribution for the year. Since 1995 the United States has donated a total of $60.4 million.
The aid is intended to combat widespread malnutrition, particularly among children, caused by several years of severe flooding that compounded the problems of North Korea's hardline communist system.
